source.title: Towards the Memorization Effect of Neural Networks in Adversarial Training
source.authors: Han Xu; Xiaorui Liu; Wentao Wang; Wen-Biao Ding; Zhong-Qin Wu; Zitao Liu; Anil K. Jain; Ji-Liang Tang

record.tranche_reason: Studies the effect of fitting atypical, high-memorization-value samples during adversarial training, an extension beyond the claim’s standard-training settings.
record.gate_note: The study varies how many atypical samples are included during training and reports test-set results. It does not test random-label fitting, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness, or random-removal controls.
record.test_reason: The study investigates a related question: how fitting high-memorization examples affects typical- and atypical-subset performance under adversarial training. It does not test V8's comparison of removing highly memorized examples against removing equally many random examples. Its other experiments do not test V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: fitting atypical examples during adversarial training improves atypical clean accuracy but contributes little to atypical robustness, and can harm typical-subset performance. The authors use these findings to motivate BAT's improved clean-accuracy versus robustness trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: Studies atypical-sample inclusion and test performance in adversarial training, rather than the claim’s standard-training random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or removal-versus-random comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects differ between traditional ERM and adversarial training, and between typical-sample clean accuracy and atypical-sample clean or adversarial accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Under CIFAR100 adversarial training, including atypical examples reduces ResNet18 typical-subset clean accuracy from 92% to 85% and adversarial accuracy from 52% to 44%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Including high-memorization training examples can harm typical-subset performance under adversarial training.

fits_no_version.finding: Under traditional ERM, including atypical examples does not degrade typical-subset clean accuracy across the reported datasets and architectures; CIFAR100 accuracy is slightly higher with all included.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of including high-memorization examples on typical-subset accuracy depends on the training objective.

fits_no_version.finding: During CIFAR100 adversarial training, test atypical clean accuracy approaches 40%, while atypical adversarial accuracy stays around 10% despite high training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting atypical examples during adversarial training accompanies improved clean generalization to atypical examples but little improvement in their robustness.

record.problems: The study reports no equal-count random-removal control for the tested atypical-sample comparisons. Some additional results are presented only in figures, without exact values in the text. The reported main comparisons concern adversarial training and subset-specific test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: The paper’s BAT-versus-baseline tables compare the authors’ proposed adversarial-training method with other methods, not the claim’s memorization object. Other figure-only atypical-set performance results in Figures 1, 2, 9–14 and 19–20 are not extracted because they do not provide a direct removal-versus-random comparison for V8.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training and held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Whether removing highly memorized examples lowers overall clean test accuracy more than equal-count random removal; dataset dependence including MNIST.

record.verdict_notes: Missing random-removal controls are an untested comparison, not evidence limiting or challenging V8. The omitted atypical-set curves are already declared in rows_left_out. Subset-specific harm does not establish that removing atypical examples improves overall test accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The study varies inclusion of atypical samples, but does not compare removing the most memorized examples with removing an equal number of random examples; most reported test measures are restricted to typical or atypical subsets.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the typical training set with 0% versus 100% of atypical samples included.
rows.measure: Clean accuracy on the test typical set
rows.note: The comparison tests atypical-sample inclusion under adversarial training; it is not a comparison against removing an equal number of random training examples.
rows.check: The 92% versus 85% clean accuracies are correctly reported, but concern only the selected typical test subset, without an equal-count random-removal control. They cannot establish V8's comparative removal effect.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the typical training set with 0% versus 100% of atypical samples included.
rows.measure: Adversarial accuracy on the test typical set
rows.note: The result is for adversarial accuracy on typical samples, not overall test accuracy.
rows.check: The 52% versus 44% values are correct, but measure adversarial accuracy on typical test samples, rather than V8's clean test-accuracy removal comparison.

rows.subject: Traditional ERM models under ResNet18 and WRN28
rows.operation_detail: Trained with different amounts of atypical samples included; test typical-set clean accuracy was compared.
rows.measure: Clean accuracy on the test typical set
rows.value: With 100% atypical samples, accuracy was even slightly higher than with 0% in CIFAR100; the text says the conclusion was consistent across all three datasets and model architectures.
rows.note: The text describes the direction, but does not state exact values. This is a natural-training comparison; no equal-count random-removal comparison is reported.
rows.check: Typical-subset clean accuracy without a random-removal comparator cannot establish absence of V8's effect. Split datasets and architectures; Tiny ImageNet figure captions identify ResNet32, whereas the appendix's general setup says ResNet18.

rows.subject: ResNet18 and WRN28
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the typical training set with varying portions of atypical samples included.
rows.measure: Clean and adversarial accuracy on the test typical set
rows.value: With 100% atypical samples, clean and adversarial accuracy dropped by ∼ 7% and 8%, respectively.
rows.note: The reported drops concern test typical samples; the text gives no random-removal control.
rows.check: This combines architectures and two measures and overlaps R1–R2. The approximately 7- and 8-percentage-point drops are stated for CIFAR100 generally; the text does not separately assign those exact drops to WRN28. These are typical-subset results without random-removal controls.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR100 ResNet18 under adversarial training; test typical samples
reader_labels.reason: Including atypical samples is associated with lower typical-set clean and adversarial accuracy (R1, R2); the study lacks the version’s equal-count random-removal comparison and does not establish an overall test-accuracy effect.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Traditional ERM, CIFAR100, CIFAR10 and Tiny ImageNet; test typical samples
reader_labels.reason: The text reports no degradation from including atypical samples in these comparisons, with CIFAR100 accuracy slightly higher at 100% inclusion (R3); exact figure values and random-removal controls are absent.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR100 under adversarial training; test typical samples
reader_labels.reason: Across ResNet18 and WRN28, the text reports ∼ 7% and 8% drops in clean and adversarial accuracy with all atypical samples included (R4), but does not compare with random removals.
